C01.why: Uniforms and flashlight skins are visible to your crew, and a revive offered as either a rewarded video or a paid product is a proven horror lever (as in DOORS). But nights are dark, so self-expression is hard to see, and the pitch has no persistent space to customize that other players can see.
C01.fix: Make the motel lobby a persistent shared space that each player can decorate, with decor bundles and uniform sets the whole crew sees between nights and that can be gifted to friends. Cap the paid revive at once per night, with the rewarded-video revive always offered next to it.

C02.why: Rounds are 90 seconds and attention stays on the device, so outfits barely register, and the functional emotes must stay free. Matchmaking with strangers weakens social buying, leaving only thin cosmetic SKUs (confetti colours, device skins).
C02.fix: Sell squad cosmetic sets: one buyer reskins the whole team's device and blast effect for the session, with the buyer named on it, and the set can be gifted. Add a paid 'Workshop' for building custom device challenges and sharing them by code.

C03.why: Vehicles are a natural purchase: new thruster layouts are fair sidegrades, and Roblox vehicle games sell cars well. Wake trails and skins on the one shared raft are highly visible. Free private servers for Plus members weaken the private-lobby angle.
C03.fix: Add a 'Captain' rule: the lobby host's owned raft and skin are used for the whole team, so a purchase is shown to everyone and invites gifting. Sell premium chassis that are also earnable, so the purchase is a shortcut to variety and never to power.

C04.why: The shop-tycoon frame supports proven purchases: shop decor and themes, museum display cases as a showcase of collection prestige, and convenience passes. The persistent shop is self-expression that friends can visit. The tool-tier speed-ups risk becoming pay-to-progress if they can be bought outright.
C04.fix: Keep tool tiers earn-only and sell cosmetic tool variants instead. Add visitable player museums with paid premium display cases and plaques, plus a giftable 'Collector's Wing', so whales can spend on showing off without any advantage.

C05.why: Strong visibility: the Parent costume is the focus of every round, and chaos effects (paint colours, smash VFX) are public. Asymmetric games can sell a role-priority pass but players resent it. Rounds are short, there is no persistent space, and there is no recurring pass.
C05.fix: Sell signature 'chaos finishers', such as a custom paint-splat colour or a smash sound, that every player sees when they cause the biggest mess. Add a cosmetic-only season pass with Parent costumes as the headline rewards. Keep role selection fair through rotation, with no paid priority.

C06.why: Incrementals have the highest raw conversion of these genres (auto-forks, 2x passes, boosts). But players compete over the shared pile, so a paid boost directly costs other players needles, which creates pay-to-win friction. Simulators are also the loops Roblox now down-ranks and the FTC complaint targets.
C06.fix: Change boosts to server-wide social purchases: a 'Hay Storm' benefits everyone, and the buyer gets credit and a cosmetic trophy plaque. Make needle odds independent of paid power, and sell machine skins for plots that other players can see.

C07.why: Outfits, rope colours and photo frames are visible but low-value. The obby genre's main earner, paid stage skips, would break shared co-op progress, so the remaining spend is thin cosmetics. Gear sidegrades help a little.
C07.fix: Build a summit photo studio with paid poses, frames and filters, so photos become a cosmetic outlet. Add a basecamp hub players can customize, plus a cosmetic season pass whose rewards are tied to each daily peak.

C08.why: The montage theatre is an unusually good showcase: your outfit and camera are replayed to the lobby, and the channel studio is persistent self-expression. Gear progression could slide into pay-to-progress, and the haunted levels are dark.
C08.fix: Sell channel branding (intro stingers, logos, montage filters and transitions) that plays to everyone in the theatre, and make studios visitable. Keep camera gear earn-only and sell cosmetic variants of it.

C09.why: Spell-colour effects are cast constantly and are highly visible, robes and staffs are standard PvE cosmetics, and tower-defence players accept sidegrade content. Ten-minute sessions and four players limit social pressure to buy.
C09.fix: Sell 'ink' rune-trail and combo-VFX cosmetics that change how shared combos look (for example a firenado in your colour). Add a cosmetic battle pass, and sell rune-book sidegrade schools that can also be earned.

C10.why: Creature collection and breeding is Roblox's most proven spending category, as Adopt Me and Creatures of Sonaria show. Nest slots, critter cosmetics, family-tree prestige and pairing with a friend's critter give natural convenience and social purchases. The risk is paid randomness around mutations, which needs disclosed odds and is blocked in some regions.
C10.fix: Never sell random mutations or eggs. Sell deterministic accessories, nest themes and lineage-name banners, and make critters giftable to friends, so all revenue stays region-safe and free of FTC-style timers.

C11.why: The expedition pass gives recurring revenue, and suits and flashlights are standard. But play happens in dark liminal spaces with low visibility, and gear tiers and haul insurance tempt pay-to-progress.
C11.fix: Make suit cosmetics emissive and glowing so they read in the dark, make the hub a showcase where your extracted artifacts are on display, and keep gear earn-only.

C12.why: Aircraft and liveries follow the proven vehicle-game model, and the livery is visible to the whole crew. Crew emotes are a modest extra. Selling aircraft that unlock new emergency types locks gameplay behind payment.
C12.fix: Make aircraft earnable but sell premium ones and livery editors as shortcuts. Add a 'Captain's aircraft' rule so the host's owned plane flies for the whole crew, which encourages gifting.

C13.why: Territory skins and capital monuments are seen by 50 players every match, clans enable pooled and social buying, and a season pass gives recurring revenue. But on the 2D map avatars barely appear, so the R15 adult DevEx bonus is weak, and any paid troop advantage would kill the game.
C13.fix: Add clan treasuries where members can donate Robux toward clan banners and map skins everyone sees. Sell animated territory patterns and 'victory monument' effects that play to all 50 players at the end of a match.

C14.why: Van skins, uniforms and parcel wrap are visible but generic. Delivery sims monetize moderately through vehicle sales. There is no recurring pass or social purchase, and selling van upgrades risks pay-to-progress.
C14.fix: Sell 'signature deliveries': premium parcel wraps and customer-reaction effects shown to the whole team when a delivery is perfect. Add an agency HQ to customize and a cosmetic courier pass.

C15.why: The TFT model fits: every opponent sees your board, toy skins create many items to sell, and a battle pass plus ranked play give recurring cosmetic spending, as RIVALS shows. Toy unlocks are earned, so the economy stays fair. The genre's niche audience caps the upside.
C15.fix: Sell a 'little legend'-style avatar commander and knockout finisher effects, shown to the eliminated player, with direct purchase only and no eggs, so it stays region-safe.

C16.why: Rewarded video and home or van cosmetics are weak, and there is no avatar showcase, competitive flex or persistent social space. Timed chores also invite FTC-style pressure if a paid time extension is ever added.
C16.fix: Give every player a customizable companion pet that comes on jobs, with accessories, tricks and gifting, and a visitable agency HQ.

C17.why: Piece skins and tower themes are the only options. Pieces are shared and short-lived, so ownership is hard to show off, and versus play rules out paid power.
C17.fix: Add a 'signature piece' that each buyer drops once per match with their name on it, team tower themes chosen by the host, and a cosmetic battle pass.

C18.why: Collective server purchases, such as cosmetics donated to the shared monster with a contributor leaderboard, are a strong whale and social lever with high visibility. Capped boosts that feed the Saturday cross-server battle are pay-to-win and will cause resentment, and individual self-expression is weak.
C18.fix: Make monster purchases cosmetic only, credited on the monster with a plaque naming the donor. Sell personal 'keeper' gear and roles that are cosmetic, and remove boosts from the battle stats.

C19.why: Statue skins clash with the core mechanic: a rare paid skin makes you stand out among the NPC statues, which turns a purchase into a handicap. Guard costumes and poses are fine but thin.
C19.fix: When a player equips a paid skin, add matching NPC statues for that round so skins act as disguise packs. Sell mischief-effect cosmetics, such as a moustache style or prank VFX, that are seen when the guard discovers the prank.

C20.why: Cosmetics and ball trails in a competitive sport work on paper, but Volleyball Legends already holds the audience and the spending (through style spins). Without a battle pass or team purchases, a cosmetic-only newcomer will monetize weakly.
C20.fix: Add a cosmetic ranked season pass, squad jersey bundles that one player can buy for the whole team, and spike and serve impact effects visible to the whole court.

overall_notes: Few Roblox players spend (about 3.8%) and median ARPPU is about $0.70, so cosmetic-only co-op games mostly earn through visibility (effects seen by everyone, persistent spaces friends can visit) and social purchases (host or captain items applied to the whole squad, gifting). These are missing from most pitches. The strongest fits are proven categories that keep spending free of frustration: C10 breeding and collection (if randomness is never sold), C04 a shop and museum players can visit, and C15 boards seen by every opponent plus a pass. Concepts whose obvious earner hurts play are capped: paid boosts in shared or competitive spaces (C06, C18), skips in co-op climbing (C07), and paid skins that expose hiders (C19). Plus members now get free private servers, so private lobbies are no longer a revenue lever. The +42% adult DevEx bonus helps only R15 avatar-forward games, and C13 does not qualify. Avoid paid timers, limited-time pressure and paid random items in every concept, because of the FTC complaint and regional blocks.
